For Petitioner : Mr. Akhtar Hussain , Advocate For State : Mr. Chitendra Singh, P.L.
 Hon'ble Shri Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey  ORDER 18.10.2023 1 The petitioner has challenged the Order passed by the learned Trial Court dated 14.09.2023 in Special Criminal Case No. 97/2021, whereby an application moved by the petitioner to summon the witnesses for cross-examination has been rejected on the ground that the victim and her mother were examined on 21.04.2022 and 22.04.2022 and they were extensively cross examined by counsel of the petitioner and application under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. was moved after lapse of one year on 18.04.2023.

2 The facts of the present case are that the petitioner is being tried for commission for offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376 of the IPC and 4 of the POCSO Act in Special Criminal Case which is pending before the learned Court below.
The victim was examined, the examination in chief of the victim was recorded on 21.04.2022 and on 22.04.2022, she was cross examined by the counsel of the petitioner.
Likewise, mother of the victim was examined on 21.04.2022 and 22.04.2022 and she was also cross examined.
3 On 18.04.2023, an application was moved by the petitioner to summon the victim and her mother as some relevant questions could not be put forth during the course of cross examination.
It is also stated in the application that earlier counsel before Court below could not put relevant questions to them, therefore, application may be allowed.
The learned Trial Court after taking into consideration the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the reasons assigned in the application, rejected it.

4 The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that an application moved by the petitioner under Section 311 of the Cr.P.C.
ought to have been allowed by the learned Court below.
He would further submit that the cross examination of the witnesses is right of an accused and it cannot be denied.

sentences.text: 1 relevant questions could not be put forth and, therefore, an opportunity may be given to the petitioner.
5 On the other hand, learned counsel for the State would oppose.
6 I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents.

7 The provisions of Section 33(5) of the POCSO Act reads as under:-
"The Special Court shall ensure that the child is not called repeatedly to testify in the court".
8 In the matter of Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana and others passed in SLP (Crl) No. 1258 of 2022 on 29.08.2023 observed as under:-

entities.text: Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Manju Devi v State of Rajasthan, (2019) 6 SCC 203, this Court emphasized that a discretionary power like Section 311, CrPC is to enable the Court to keep the record straight and to clear any ambiguity regarding the evidence, whilst also ensuring no prejudice is caused to anyone.

entities.text: Manju Devi v State of Rajasthan, (2019) 6 SCC 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A note of caution was sounded in Swapan Kumar Chatterjee v Central Bureau of Investigation, (2019) 14 SCC 328 as under: The first part of this section which is permissive gives purely discretionary authority to the criminal court and enables it at any stage of in- quiry, trial or other proceedings under the Code to act in one of the three ways, namely, (i) to summon any person as a witness; or (ii) to examine any per- son in attendance, though not summoned as a witness; or (iii) to recall and re- examine any person already examined.

entities.text: Swapan Kumar Chatterjee v Central Bureau of Investigation, (2019) 14 SCC 328
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The second part, which is mandatory, imposes an obligation on the court (i) to summon and examine or (ii) to recall and re-examine any such person if his evidence appears to be essential to the just decision of the case.
11. It is well settled that the power conferred under Section 311 should be invoked by the court only to meet the ends of justice.
The power is to be exercised only for strong and valid reasons and it should be exercised with great caution and circumspection.

The court has vide power under this section to even recall witnesses for re-examination or further examination, necessary in the interest of justice, but the same has to be exercised after taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of each case.
The power under this provision shall not be exercised if the court is of the view that the application has been filed as an abuse of the process of law.

12. Where the prosecution evidence has been closed long back and the reasons for non- examination of the witness earlier are not satisfactory, the summoning of the witness at belated stage would cause great prejudice to the accused and should not be allowed.
Similarly, the court should not encourage the filing of successive applications for recall of a witness under this provision".

9 Coming to the facts of the present case in the light of judgment passed in Satbir Singh (supra) by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is quite vivid that the victim and her mother were examined on 21.04.2022 and cross examined on 22.04.2022, thereafter, the application under Section 311 of the Rahul @ Santu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95798988/
2 Cr.P.C. was moved on 08.04.2023 by the petitioner to cross-examine the witnesses and assigning the reason of change of the counsel.

sentences.text: 10 Considering the fact that as per the provisions of Section 33(5) POCSO Act, the victim is not required to call repeatedly to testify in the court.

Further, the application was moved after lapse of one year without explaining any reason and it is well settled that the power conferred under Section 311 CrPC should be invoked by the court only to meet the ends of justice and has to be exercised only for strong and valid reasons and it should be exercised with great caution and circumspection
, in the opinion of this Court, the learned Court below has not committed any error of law in rejecting the application.
11 Accordingly, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.

Sd/-
(Rakesh Mohan Pandey) Judge sourabh.
